claim: The VESTA20H grids are in Claudia Double Prime: drawn at Claudia longitude + 150 degrees (Claudia - 210) they line up with the DLR HAMO terrain and Gazetteer features of the Claudia-frame maps.

method.terrain: Pearson r between the DLR HAMO radius (Claudia, sampled 1 degree) and each gravity grid sampled at Claudia longitude + shift, |lat|<=60, rows demeaned, cos-lat weights. Terrain read with the shared PDS scalar-grid reader at 361 x 181 points; grids with the draft pds3-grid reader. Run 2026-09-28 on f01a41ff00 plus this change.
method.features: Bouguer value at IAU/USGS Gazetteer centres (Claudia Double Prime, as the grid) and 210 degrees away; percentile among all cells.

reference: Raymond et al. (2013), EGU2013-12408, https://meetingorganizer.copernicus.org/EGU2013/EGU2013-12408.pdf: large positive Bouguer anomaly at Vestalia Terra at the western intersection of the Rheasilvia and Veneneia basins, a weaker positive over the central mound of Rheasilvia, a positive over the equatorial troughs at the north-eastern edge of Rheasilvia, negative anomalies over most of Veneneia.
notes: The Bouguer maximum, 238.23 mGal at 11 E 32 S (Claudia Double Prime), lies inside the Gazetteer extent of Vestalia Terra (0.3 to 75.9 E, 32.4 S to 23.6 N), 6.6 degrees outside the Rheasilvia rim and 7.7 degrees outside the Veneneia rim (rims from the Gazetteer centres and diameters on a 265 km sphere).
At the Veneneia centre the grid reads -1.0 mGal (48th percentile), not the negative the abstract describes; 210 degrees away it reads -99.7.
The mean over the whole Vestalia Terra box does not separate the two placements (-11.1 against -12.3 mGal).
